_about: Artifact-side ledger: what each build 'contains, how big it is, what the probes read'. Pairs with official_ledger.json (the official-account side).
_what_this_is: The corpus is the official nightly builds of **llama.cpp (ggml-org)** — b10472 / b10595 / b11681. These are inference-engine binaries, **not Meta's Llama model weights**; the llama-b<number>/ directory name easily suggests a model, but the case is about engine binaries.
_why_this_file_exists: This case's corpus is 713 MB × 3 = 2.1 GB of official binaries; it cannot go into git and cannot be distributed with the repository. So the **measured artifact-side facts** are pinned here: even a reader without the corpus can check 'the readout I see matches what you recorded'.
_honesty_boundary: ★ This file is a **measured record**, not the evidence itself. It lets a reader check readout consistency, but **it cannot replace re-running the probes** — only a run against the real binaries counts as verification. That is why fetch_corpus.py has to exist: if you can re-download, do not trust this ledger alone.
_generated_by: fetch_corpus.py --manifest (rescans the real builds and overwrites this file)
_platform_observed: Windows x64; CUDA 13 family (major 13 inferred from the cublas64_13.dll / ggml-cuda.dll shipped inside the artifacts, not stated in any document). ★ The exact minor version differs per build: b10472/b10595 = cuda-13.3, b11681 = cuda-13.4 — pin the official release asset names, do not write a vague 'CUDA 13'.
_cuda_evidence: The major version 13 is inferred from the shipped DLLs; the minor 13.3/13.4 is pinned by the official release asset names (llama-b<tag>-bin-win-cuda-<minor>-x64.zip) checked against GitHub metadata. These are evidence of different strength: the DLL only proves 'this family', the minor version is anchored by the asset name.
_pin_source: GitHub release asset metadata (collected 2026-10-28): sha256 digests from the releases/expanded_assets/<tag> page plus the Content-Length of a HEAD request to each asset download URL. ★ The 450 MB corpus was not downloaded; byte counts are measured HEAD values, not the page's rounded display (the page shows 146,707,438 as 140 MB).
_pin_api_fallback: The REST API (api.github.com/.../releases/tags/<tag>) returned 403 rate limit at the time, so digests were taken from the sha256 badges in the GitHub release page's expanded_assets fragment (aria-label='Copy to clipboard digest'), and byte counts from the HEAD Content-Length of the download URLs. Both are GitHub server-side metadata; no archive was downloaded.

asset_pins._about: Official release asset names + exact bytes + SHA256. ★ Measured: b10472/b10595 are cuda-13.3, b11681 is cuda-13.4 — **the minor version differs within the same 'CUDA 13' family**; never write a vague 'CUDA 13'.
asset_pins._verification: After download, fetch_corpus.py checks used_asset_bytes + used_asset_sha256; a mismatch refuses to unpack. An existing bad file is removed and re-downloaded.
asset_pins._total_used_asset_note: The three cuda assets total 447,813,339 bytes (about 448 MB / 427 MiB). With `--asset cpu` the total is 56,172,043 bytes (about 56 MB / 54 MiB), but the cpu readout is unverified.

corpus_status._about: ★ An honest record of the corpus state. The case's readout was measured in the state below.
corpus_status.reason: the two older builds were deleted after the verification run passed
corpus_status.impact: ★ **the cross-version conclusion cannot be re-run**. The disappearance of template-analysis is a cross-version comparison (present in b10472/b10595 → absent in b11681); with only after and no before, the `C3` account loses its comparison object.
corpus_status.how: python fetch_corpus.py (re-download from the official release, see asset_pins; each zip is checked against its exact bytes + SHA256 before unpacking)
corpus_status._why_record_this: A discipline of this project: **a missing corpus must be recorded, not worked around**. This entry is itself teaching material for the case — it shows what to leave behind when 'the build is gone'. Without it, later readers would assume all three builds were always there, and when a re-run produces no conclusion they would not know what to blame.

C1_server_has_SLOTS_N_DIFF.note: the official statement introduced it only in b10595; a build earlier than that should not have it

key_file_sizes._about: ★ Sizes are recorded to pin the 'stub vs impl' trap: llama-server.exe is a 9216-byte shell, the real code is in llama-server-impl.dll (9259520 bytes), a factor of 1000. Checking the wrong file gives an all-False false readout.

C3_template_analysis_present.note: ★ missing — the core finding of this case

sibling_stub_sizes._note: The other exes in the same directory are also 9216-byte stubs, recorded together to show this is a systematic structure, not an isolated case

core_finding._statement: llama-template-analysis.exe was removed in b11681, and the official release notes for the three versions say not one word about it.
core_finding._evidence: present in b10472/b10595 → missing in b11681; the body_details_verbatim of all three versions in official_ledger.json mentions only 'additions', with no removal record at all.
core_finding._engine_reading: C3 is judged an outlier (1/3 = 33.3%), and triggers 2 cross-version ratchet violations, all at b11681.
core_finding._caveat: Removal is not necessarily bad (it may be a deliberate cleanup). That it **went unannounced** is a fact; **the removal itself** is another matter — the two must be stated separately.
